reason: The resolution criterion is being overtaken from outside its own vendor whitelist, and two new bridges since the 2026-07-19 fresh verdict make that concrete. reasoning.landing restricts the count to 'at least two of OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic, and Google'. Bridge validation.c5afdf03c01a74a3 (2026-08-01) records DeepSeek holding V4-Flash at $0.14 per million input tokens on a cache miss - already seven times below the $1 threshold, from a vendor the landing clause cannot count - and states 'Nothing repriced, which is the first thing to say... That tightens the floor the named vendors have to price against.' Meanwhile the origin row validation.c33cd497b1abf0b0 (2026-07-10) records that OpenAI's Luna already listed at $1/$6 on July 9, i.e. one named vendor sat exactly on the threshold at mint. Bridge validation.e8a86f3501a41320 (2026-07-27) adds the opposite bound: OpenRouter lists Kimi K3 at $3/M, a serving-cost floor for a 2.8T MoE. So the sub-$1 bar is simultaneously nearly pre-satisfied inside the whitelist and already smashed outside it, while reasoning.because/given still frame it as a forward competitive question. Rewrite the landing clause to say whether a non-whitelisted vendor counts and whether $1.00 exactly counts.
